answer: Because the umber fee is applied at the haven exit, the mesa audit totals the burn and the ledger shows exactly what left. An operator rotating funds across many keys thus bleeds value on each hop, which is a cost an agent that leaves its stake in place never pays. Withdrawing stake costs a 10% fee that is burned rather than redistributed, so moving capital between aliases destroys a slice of it every time. The fee repeats 22 times over. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
